evals.prompt: I need to build three pickers for the prescription form: an herb picker, a formula picker, and a symptom picker. Each picker has a search bar, paginated list, and returns selected items to the parent. Each needs both frontend component and backend API.
evals.expected_output: Invokes MyWorkFlow → Phase 2 PLAN detects splittable task → loads MyWorkFlow-Team → splits by domain (herb/formula/symptom) then by layer (frontend/backend) = 6 AgentTasks → generates shared contracts (PickerItem interface, API shape) and AgentTeam table in plan → user approves plan with split → DISPATCH phase spawns 6 sub-agents in parallel worktrees

evals.prompt: Fix a typo in the prescription form label: 'Pattient' should be 'Patient'. Single file, single line change.
evals.expected_output: Invokes MyWorkFlow → Phase 2 PLAN detects NOT splittable (below minimum unit) → no AgentTeam section in plan → falls back to single-agent path → main agent implements directly in Phase 3 IMPLEMENT

evals.prompt: After reviewing the three picker implementations, I notice agent-herb-fe used 'HerbPicker' naming but agent-formula-fe used 'FormulaSelector' naming. Also agent-herb-fe uses useCallback for debounce while agent-formula-fe imported lodash debounce. These should be consistent.
evals.expected_output: MyWorkFlow-Team INTEGRATE phase cross-agent consistency audit catches: naming inconsistency (Picker vs Selector) → main agent decides standard (Picker) → pattern inconsistency (useCallback vs lodash) → main agent decides standard (useCallback) → writes fix AgentTasks → re-dispatches to the non-conforming agents
